title: invocation.v1
description: The meeting-bot's constructor — delivered as one JSON env var VEXA_BOT_CONFIG (ADR-0002), validated at boot. A config contract legitimately carries the secrets the bot needs (marked SECRET below; placeholders in goldens, P14). No tenancy fields (deferred, ADR-0003).

VoiceNote.description: A voice note: no meeting to join. The person's browser streams capture.v1 audio frames through the gateway to meeting-api, which appends each one to `audioStream`; the bot reads that stream in order and runs it through the same pipeline a meeting's audio takes. Present exactly when `platform` is `voice_note`

audioStream.description: the Redis stream the bot reads (XREAD), `voice_note:meeting:{meeting_id}:audio`. Each entry is one capture.v1 audio frame (field `f`) or the end of the note (field `end`)

maxDurationSec.description: the longest note, in seconds of audio. meeting-api accepts no audio past it; the bot ends a note still running a minute later with `max_bot_time_exceeded`

idleTimeoutSec.description: how long the bot waits with neither audio nor an end before it ends the note (`left_alone`): the browser went away without Stop

speakerName.description: the name the note's words are attributed to (the person recording); absent ⇒ the lane's unnamed label

Call.description: A Vexa call: a room on the deployment's self-hosted LiveKit server. The bot joins it hidden and subscribe-only and reads each participant's microphone track (and, unless `screenShareAudio` is false, the audio of a screen they share) as its own channel, named by the participant; no browser. Present exactly when `platform` is `vexa_call`

url.description: the LiveKit server as the bot reaches it inside the deployment

room.description: the room name meeting-api minted for this call

token.description: SECRET — the listener's LiveKit access token: hidden, subscribe-only, this room only, expiring with the call's cap. Placeholder in goldens

maxDurationSec.description: the longest call; the bot ends a call still running at it with `max_bot_time_exceeded`

emptyGraceSec.description: how long an emptied room is given for someone to come back before the call ends (`left_alone`)

firstJoinTimeoutSec.description: how long the bot waits for the first participant before the call ends (`left_alone`)

screenShareAudio.description: policy: also transcribe the audio of a screen a participant shares (a tab or video with sound), as its own channel named "<participant> (shared screen)"; false ⇒ that track is never read (CALL_TRANSCRIBE_SHARED_SCREEN)

meetingUrl.description: null for native-SDK zoom, for voice_note (nothing to join) for vexa_call (the room is in `call`) and for discord (a voice channel is joined by nativeMeetingId, not a URL)

passcode.description: meeting passcode (zoom passcode screen / jitsi room password); placeholder in goldens

token.description: SECRET — the session's MeetingToken and the bot's only credential: an HS256 token meeting-api mints per spawn, bound to this session's connectionId (claim session_uid). It is the transport bearer, `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, at four doors: every lifecycle.v1 event the bot POSTs to meetingApiCallbackUrl, every upload to recordingUploadUrl, an authenticated bot's session-profile.v1 write-back to sessionWritebackUrl, and its restore from sessionRestoreUrl; meeting-api refuses it for any other session, and requires its exp, aud and scope. Required by a meeting-api from v0.13.2: a bot that sends no bearer is refused (401). Placeholder in goldens

redisUrl.description: SECRET — the Redis URL for the acts.v1 command channel and the transcript egress, with credentials. Per-workload ACL (the default) puts a Redis user of the bot's own session in it, granted exactly: append to transcription_segments, publish on tc:meeting:{meeting_id}:mutable, subscribe to bot_commands:meeting:{meeting_id}, and the commands xadd publish subscribe unsubscribe ping quit; for a voice note also xread on its own voiceNote.audioStream and no other key; the user is removed when the session ends. With REDIS_WORKLOAD_ACL=shared it carries meeting-api's own service connection instead. Placeholder in goldens

internalSecret.description: DEPRECATED, MUST NOT be set. A producer from v0.13.2 never sends it and a bot ignores it: the bot authenticates with `token`. It stays in the schema only so a bot can still parse an invocation from an older meeting-api

transcriptionModel.description: stt model id sent as the OpenAI-compatible `model` form part; unset → whisper-1

transcriptionServiceOwner.description: who operates transcriptionServiceUrl. `customer` (the person's own Settings endpoint) holds every bot request to it to the outbound URL guard: refused when it names or resolves to an internal or private address, and dialled at the checked address. Absent or `vexa`: the deployment's own endpoint, which may be private. Sent by a meeting-api from v0.13.2, and only as `customer`; a bot older than v0.13.2 refuses an invocation that carries it

captureSignalEnabled.description: tee the raw captured-signal.v1 stream (audio frames + speaker events) to durable storage for offline replay (O-TEL-1); the transcript/recording paths are unaffected either way

sessionWritebackUrl.description: an authenticated bot's session write-back sink: the full URL, session uid included, the bot PUTs its session-profile.v1 WritebackBody to on clean teardown, with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Sent by a meeting-api from v0.13.2, and only beside `authenticated`; absent, the bot writes nothing back and derives no URL. A bot older than v0.13.2 refuses an invocation that carries it

sessionRestoreUrl.description: an authenticated bot's session source when its profile is a saved bot account rather than the userdata store: the full URL, session uid included, the bot GETs before launch with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the answer is a session-profile.v1 WritebackBody, and the bot writes only its SESSION_PROFILE paths into its profile dir. Any failure is fail-loud (the session-restore failure, as for the store). Sent only beside `authenticated`; absent, the bot restores from the store or not at all and derives no URL. A bot that predates the field refuses an invocation that carries it

meetingHostAllow.description: the operator's meeting-host allowance (meeting-api `VEXA_MEETING_HOST_ALLOW`): exact host names and IP networks (CIDR) inside the operator's network that the bot's navigations may reach, such as an on-prem Jitsi. Every navigation and redirect of the bot's browser must stay on the platform's hosts or the meeting's own host and resolve to a public address; a listed name or network is also admitted when it resolves privately, never to loopback, link-local/cloud metadata, unspecified, multicast or reserved addresses. Sent only when the operator listed entries; a bot that predates the field refuses an invocation that carries it
